text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: auth-proxy error spike (500s) from a small set of client IPs. 2,300 auth failures in 5m, abnormal token refresh rate. Detected anomaly score 0.87. Root request example attached.

maria: seeing this on my dashboard too. top IPs are 18.200.45.12 and 34.121.9.4, both hitting /v1/auth/refresh.

ben: can we throttle those IPs at the edge? @carmen are we able to add quick firewall block?

carmen: yes we can add a temporary deny rule on the infra WAF. I will push a block to the network ACLs for those two IPs in 2m. doing it now.

carmen: applied WAF deny for 18.200.45.12 and 34.121.9.4 :lock: please verify traffic.

maria: traffic from those IPs dropped to near 0 after the rule. auth failures down 82% in the last minute. good stop.

ben: summary so far: high-volume token refresh failures -> suspicious retry pattern -> blocked at WAF. Next: are tokens compromised or misuse? need to revoke affected sessions and rotate any leaked keys.

maria: pulling logs to identify impacted service accounts. running query:
```
# Kibana
source:auth-proxy AND status:401 AND event:refresh_token AND src_ip:(18.200.45.12 OR 34.121.9.4) | top user_id,client_id
```

maria: returned ~520 distinct user_ids across 3 customer orgs; ~40 service-account tokens. Looks like one service account's refresh key being replayed.

devon: @security-bot can we escalate to SecOps for key rotation guidance?

security-bot: Escalation created: SEC-2026-031. Suggested immediate actions:
- Revoke service-account refresh tokens for affected SA IDs
- Rotate any long-lived keys attached to those SAs
- Block outbound egress for containers that matched the pattern until further notice
- Notify affected customers via CS with template SEC-2026-031.

ben: I'll take service-account revocation. running script to list sessions and revoke refresh tokens for the ~40 SAs.

ben: command used:
```
# revoke refresh tokens
for sa in $(cat sa_list.txt); do
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
    https://api.redwood.example/v1/admin/revoke_refresh -d "{\"service_account\":\"$sa\"}" || echo $sa >> revoke_failures.txt
done
```

maria: started a job to rotate KMS keys for any S3 artifacts uploaded by the suspected SAs. Will coordinate with storage team.

carmen: Ops note: deployed a temporary rate-limit policy on auth-proxy route /v1/auth/refresh (100r/m per IP) to reduce blast radius.

devon: Pete from Support, please prepare a customer notification for the three orgs we saw activity in. Minimal impact right now, tokens revoked for the service accounts we flagged.

ops-night: taking handoff for overnight monitoring. I will keep the WAF block active and monitor auth failure rate every 15m. If it spikes again, I'll escalate to on-call SRE.

maria: tagging runbook entries: incident runbook page -> section "auth token replay" updated with commands and KMS rotation checklist. Link: https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/auth-replay

ben: logs show no sign of data exfil; S3 access patterns are normal besides the service account uploads. storage confirmed no large GETs.

carmen: we should still rotate any keys that exist in plaintext in logs. found one debug log pattern that included partial token (redacted) — we've clipped log retention and are purging accidental debug snapshots. initiating log redaction job now.

devon: customer impact assessment: three customers had transient failed refreshes; two experienced token invalidation for one morning window while we revoked SAs (some automated processes might need new creds). CS will send instructions for reconnecting. No data leaked confirmed.

security-bot: Recommended follow-ups:
- Full audit of service-account key creation patterns (past 90d)
- Add anomaly detector for abnormal refresh volumes per SA
- Harden auth-proxy to reject refreshes signed with deprecated algorithm variants
- Add automated rotation for long-lived SAs older than 30d

ops-night: leaving a short checklist for next on-call:
- keep WAF rule enforced for 24h
- run auth-failure summary hourly
- confirm KMS rotations completed by morning
- escalate if failures > 200/min

maria: closing notes before handoff: actions taken: WAF deny, rate-limit, revoked ~40 service-account refresh tokens, kicked off KMS rotation, started log redaction, CS notified. Root cause under investigation (likely leaked SA key). No confirmed customer data exfiltration.

ops-night: acknowledged handoff. I'll update this thread with hourly summaries. Good job team. :thumbsup:
